about: SQLite 3.46+ (also libSQL/Turso) built-ins, merged over common.json. Math functions need a build with SQLITE_ENABLE_MATH_FUNCTIONS (on by default in the standard amalgamation).

functions.name: changes
functions.summary: Returns the number of rows inserted, updated or deleted by the most recently completed INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE on this connection.

functions.name: char
functions.summary: Returns a string made of the characters whose Unicode code points are given as arguments.

params.name: code_point
params.doc: A Unicode code point; add more arguments for more characters.

functions.name: concat
functions.summary: Concatenates the text form of every non-NULL argument; NULL arguments are skipped and all-NULL input gives an empty string (3.44+).

params.name: value
params.doc: A value to append; add more arguments to append more.

functions.name: concat_ws
functions.summary: Concatenates the non-NULL arguments after the first, placing the separator between them; returns NULL if the separator is NULL (3.44+).

params.name: separator
params.doc: Text placed between each pair of values.

params.name: value
params.doc: A value to join; NULL values are skipped. Add more arguments for more values.

functions.name: format
functions.summary: Builds a string from a printf-style format and arguments; an alias of printf (3.38+).

params.name: format
params.doc: Format string with %d, %f, %s, %q, %Q, %w, %x, %c and similar substitutions; %% writes a percent sign.

params.name: argument
params.doc: Value for the next substitution in the format.

functions.name: glob
functions.summary: Tests whether a string matches a case-sensitive Unix-style glob pattern; glob(pattern, string) is the same as string GLOB pattern. Note the pattern comes first.

params.name: pattern
params.doc: Pattern where * matches any run of characters, ? matches one character and [...] matches a character set.

params.name: string
params.doc: The value to test.

functions.name: hex
functions.summary: Returns the upper-case hexadecimal rendering of the bytes of a value, treating it as a BLOB (text uses its bytes in the database encoding).

params.name: value
params.doc: The value whose bytes to render.

functions.name: ifnull
functions.summary: Returns the first argument if it is not NULL, otherwise the second. Same as coalesce with two arguments.

params.name: value
params.doc: The value to return when it is not NULL.

params.name: fallback
params.doc: The value to return when the first is NULL.

functions.name: iif
functions.summary: Returns the second argument if the condition is true, otherwise the third; shorthand for CASE WHEN condition THEN a ELSE b END (3.32+).

params.name: condition
params.doc: The expression to test; true means non-zero and not NULL.

params.name: true_value
params.doc: Returned when the condition is true.

params.name: false_value
params.doc: Returned when the condition is false or NULL.

functions.name: instr
functions.summary: Returns the 1-based position of the first occurrence of a substring in a string, or 0 if it is not found. For BLOBs the position counts bytes.

params.name: string
params.doc: The string to search in.

params.name: substring
params.doc: The string to look for.

functions.name: last_insert_rowid
functions.summary: Returns the rowid of the most recent successful INSERT into a rowid table on this connection.

functions.name: length
functions.summary: Returns the number of characters in a string (before any NUL), the number of bytes in a BLOB, the length of a number's text form, or NULL for NULL.

params.name: value
params.doc: The string, BLOB or number to measure.

functions.name: like
functions.summary: Tests a string against a LIKE pattern; like(pattern, string) is the same as string LIKE pattern. Case-insensitive for ASCII letters by default.

params.name: pattern
params.doc: Pattern where % matches any run of characters and _ matches one character.

params.name: string
params.doc: The value to test.

params.name: escape
params.doc: A single character that makes the next % or _ in the pattern literal.

functions.name: likelihood
functions.summary: Returns its first argument unchanged while telling the query planner how likely it is to be true.

params.name: value
params.doc: The condition to pass through.

params.name: probability
params.doc: Estimated chance the value is true, a constant from 0.0 to 1.0.

functions.name: likely
functions.summary: Returns its argument unchanged while telling the query planner it is usually true; same as likelihood(value, 0.9375).

params.name: value
params.doc: The condition to pass through.

functions.name: load_extension
functions.summary: Loads an SQLite extension from a shared library file. Only works when extension loading is enabled on the connection.

params.name: file
params.doc: Path of the shared library; the platform suffix may be left out.

params.name: entry_point
params.doc: Name of the initialization function; derived from the file name when left out.

functions.name: lower
functions.summary: Returns a copy of a string with ASCII letters converted to lowercase. Non-ASCII letters are unchanged unless the ICU extension is loaded.

params.name: string
params.doc: The string to convert.

functions.name: ltrim
functions.summary: Returns a string with any of the given characters removed from its start; spaces when no characters are given.

params.name: string
params.doc: The string to trim.

params.name: characters
params.doc: Every character in this string is stripped from the left end; defaults to a space.

functions.name: max
functions.summary: With one argument, an aggregate returning the largest non-NULL value in the group. With two or more, a scalar returning the largest argument, or NULL if any argument is NULL.

params.name: expression
params.doc: The value to compare across the rows of each group; NULLs are ignored.

params.name: value1
params.doc: The first value to compare.

params.name: value2
params.doc: The next value to compare; add more arguments to compare more. Any NULL makes the result NULL.

functions.name: min
functions.summary: With one argument, an aggregate returning the smallest non-NULL value in the group. With two or more, a scalar returning the smallest argument, or NULL if any argument is NULL.

params.name: expression
params.doc: The value to compare across the rows of each group; NULLs are ignored.

params.name: value1
params.doc: The first value to compare.

params.name: value2
params.doc: The next value to compare; add more arguments to compare more. Any NULL makes the result NULL.

functions.name: octet_length
functions.summary: Returns the number of bytes in the text form of a value in the database encoding, or the number of bytes of a BLOB (3.43+).

params.name: value
params.doc: The value to measure.

functions.name: printf
functions.summary: Builds a string from a C printf-style format and arguments.

params.name: format
params.doc: Format string with %d, %f, %s, %q, %Q, %w, %x, %c and similar substitutions; %% writes a percent sign.

params.name: argument
params.doc: Value for the next substitution in the format.

functions.name: quote
functions.summary: Returns the SQL literal text for a value: strings in single quotes with quotes doubled, BLOBs as X'...' hex, NULL as the word NULL.

params.name: value
params.doc: The value to quote.

functions.name: random
functions.summary: Returns a pseudo-random 64-bit signed integer.

functions.name: randomblob
functions.summary: Returns a BLOB of the given number of pseudo-random bytes; sizes below 1 give a 1-byte BLOB.

params.name: size
params.doc: Number of random bytes to generate.

functions.name: round
functions.summary: Rounds a number to a number of digits after the decimal point, returning a floating-point value. Negative or missing digits mean 0.

params.name: number
params.doc: The value to round.

params.name: digits
params.doc: Digits to keep after the decimal point; 0 when left out or negative.

functions.name: rtrim
functions.summary: Returns a string with any of the given characters removed from its end; spaces when no characters are given.

params.name: string
params.doc: The string to trim.

params.name: characters
params.doc: Every character in this string is stripped from the right end; defaults to a space.

functions.name: sign
functions.summary: Returns -1, 0 or +1 for a negative, zero or positive number, or NULL if the argument is NULL or not a number (3.35+).

params.name: number
params.doc: The value to test.

functions.name: soundex
functions.summary: Returns the 4-character Soundex encoding of a string, or ?000 for NULL or letterless input. Only available when SQLite is built with SQLITE_SOUNDEX.

params.name: string
params.doc: The string to encode.

functions.name: sqlite_compileoption_get
functions.summary: Returns the N-th compile-time option used to build SQLite, or NULL when N is past the end.

params.name: n
params.doc: Zero-based index of the option.

functions.name: sqlite_compileoption_used
functions.summary: Returns 1 if SQLite was built with the named compile-time option, otherwise 0.

params.name: option
params.doc: Option name, with or without the SQLITE_ prefix.

functions.name: sqlite_offset
functions.summary: Returns the byte offset in the database file of the record holding a column value. Only available when built with SQLITE_ENABLE_OFFSET_SQL_FUNC.

params.name: column
params.doc: A column reference in the query.

functions.name: sqlite_source_id
functions.summary: Returns the check-in identifier and date of the SQLite source code this library was built from.

functions.name: sqlite_version
functions.summary: Returns the version of the SQLite library, such as 3.46.1.

functions.name: substr
functions.summary: Returns part of a string starting at a 1-based position; a negative start counts from the end. For BLOBs positions count bytes.

params.name: string
params.doc: The string or BLOB to take part of.

params.name: start
params.doc: 1-based starting position; negative counts back from the end.

params.name: length
params.doc: How many characters to return; to the end when left out. Negative returns the characters before start.

functions.name: substring
functions.summary: Alias of substr: returns part of a string starting at a 1-based position (3.34+). Uses commas, not FROM/FOR.

params.name: string
params.doc: The string or BLOB to take part of.

params.name: start
params.doc: 1-based starting position; negative counts back from the end.

params.name: length
params.doc: How many characters to return; to the end when left out. Negative returns the characters before start.

functions.name: total_changes
functions.summary: Returns the total number of rows inserted, updated or deleted by INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE statements since the connection was opened.

functions.name: trim
functions.summary: Returns a string with any of the given characters removed from both ends; spaces when no characters are given. SQLite uses trim(string, characters), not TRIM(BOTH ... FROM ...).

params.name: string
params.doc: The string to trim.

params.name: characters
params.doc: Every character in this string is stripped from both ends; defaults to a space.

functions.name: typeof
functions.summary: Returns the storage class of a value: 'null', 'integer', 'real', 'text' or 'blob'.

params.name: value
params.doc: The value to inspect.

functions.name: unhex
functions.summary: Decodes a hexadecimal string into a BLOB; returns NULL if it has characters that are neither hex digits nor ignorable, or an odd number of digits (3.41+).

params.name: hex
params.doc: Hex digits in pairs, upper or lower case.

params.name: ignore
params.doc: Characters allowed between digit pairs and skipped, such as spaces or dashes.

functions.name: unicode
functions.summary: Returns the Unicode code point of the first character of a string.

params.name: string
params.doc: The string whose first character to read.

functions.name: unlikely
functions.summary: Returns its argument unchanged while telling the query planner it is usually false; same as likelihood(value, 0.0625).

params.name: value
params.doc: The condition to pass through.

functions.name: upper
functions.summary: Returns a copy of a string with ASCII letters converted to uppercase. Non-ASCII letters are unchanged unless the ICU extension is loaded.

params.name: string
params.doc: The string to convert.

functions.name: zeroblob
functions.summary: Returns a BLOB of the given number of zero bytes; often used to reserve space for incremental BLOB I/O.

params.name: size
params.doc: Number of zero bytes.

functions.name: CAST
functions.summary: Converts a value using the affinity of the named type: INTEGER, REAL, TEXT, BLOB or NUMERIC. Unconvertible text becomes 0 rather than raising an error.

params.name: expression AS type_name
params.doc: The value to convert and the type whose affinity to apply, such as INTEGER, REAL, TEXT, BLOB or NUMERIC.

functions.name: avg
functions.summary: Returns the average of the non-NULL values in the group as a floating-point number, or NULL when there are none. Text that does not look like a number counts as 0.

params.name: expression
params.doc: The value to average; prefix with DISTINCT to average unique values only.

functions.name: group_concat
functions.summary: Concatenates the non-NULL values in the group into one string, separated by a comma or the given separator. Add ORDER BY inside the call to order them (3.44+).

params.name: expression
params.doc: The value to concatenate; prefix with DISTINCT for unique values.

params.name: separator
params.doc: Text placed between values; defaults to a comma.

functions.name: string_agg
functions.summary: Concatenates the non-NULL values in the group, separated by the given separator; the SQL-standard spelling of group_concat (3.44+).

params.name: expression
params.doc: The value to concatenate.

params.name: separator
params.doc: Text placed between values.

functions.name: sum
functions.summary: Adds up the non-NULL values in the group. Returns an integer when every value is an integer, NULL when there are no values, and raises an error on integer overflow.

params.name: expression
params.doc: The value to add up; prefix with DISTINCT to add unique values only.

functions.name: total
functions.summary: Adds up the non-NULL values in the group, always returning a floating-point number: 0.0 when there are no values, and never an overflow error.

params.name: expression
params.doc: The value to add up.

functions.name: json_group_array
functions.summary: Aggregate that returns a JSON array containing every value in the group, NULLs included as null.

params.name: value
params.doc: The value to add to the array.

functions.name: json_group_object
functions.summary: Aggregate that returns a JSON object built from the label/value pairs of the group.

params.name: label
params.doc: The object key for this row.

params.name: value
params.doc: The value stored under the key.

functions.name: jsonb_group_array
functions.summary: Aggregate like json_group_array, but returns the array in the binary JSONB format (3.45+).

params.name: value
params.doc: The value to add to the array.

functions.name: jsonb_group_object
functions.summary: Aggregate like json_group_object, but returns the object in the binary JSONB format (3.45+).

params.name: label
params.doc: The object key for this row.

params.name: value
params.doc: The value stored under the key.

functions.name: nth_value
functions.summary: Returns the value of an expression at the N-th row of the current window frame, or NULL when the frame has fewer rows.

params.name: expression
params.doc: The value to read.

params.name: n
params.doc: 1-based row number within the frame.

functions.name: date
functions.summary: Returns a date as text in the form YYYY-MM-DD, after applying any modifiers.

params.name: time_value
params.doc: A date/time string such as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', 'now', or a number (Julian day, or Unix time with 'unixepoch'); 'now' when left out.

params.name: modifier
params.doc: Applied left to right: '+7 days', '-3 hours', '+1 months', 'start of month', 'start of year', 'start of day', 'weekday N', 'unixepoch', 'julianday', 'auto', 'localtime', 'utc', 'subsec', 'ceiling', 'floor'.

functions.name: time
functions.summary: Returns a time as text in the form HH:MM:SS (HH:MM:SS.SSS with the subsec modifier), after applying any modifiers.

params.name: time_value
params.doc: A date/time string such as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', 'now', or a number (Julian day, or Unix time with 'unixepoch'); 'now' when left out.

params.name: modifier
params.doc: Applied left to right: '+7 days', '-3 hours', '+1 months', 'start of month', 'start of year', 'start of day', 'weekday N', 'unixepoch', 'julianday', 'auto', 'localtime', 'utc', 'subsec', 'ceiling', 'floor'.

functions.name: datetime
functions.summary: Returns a date and time as text in the form YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS, after applying any modifiers.

params.name: time_value
params.doc: A date/time string such as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', 'now', or a number (Julian day, or Unix time with 'unixepoch'); 'now' when left out.

params.name: modifier
params.doc: Applied left to right: '+7 days', '-3 hours', '+1 months', 'start of month', 'start of year', 'start of day', 'weekday N', 'unixepoch', 'julianday', 'auto', 'localtime', 'utc', 'subsec', 'ceiling', 'floor'.

functions.name: julianday
functions.summary: Returns the Julian day number (fractional days since noon in Greenwich on November 24, 4714 B.C.) for a date and time.

params.name: time_value
params.doc: A date/time string such as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', 'now', or a number (Julian day, or Unix time with 'unixepoch'); 'now' when left out.

params.name: modifier
params.doc: Applied left to right: '+7 days', '-3 hours', '+1 months', 'start of month', 'start of year', 'start of day', 'weekday N', 'unixepoch', 'julianday', 'auto', 'localtime', 'utc', 'subsec', 'ceiling', 'floor'.

functions.name: unixepoch
functions.summary: Returns the Unix timestamp (seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC) for a date and time; an integer, or real with the subsec modifier (3.38+).

params.name: time_value
params.doc: A date/time string such as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', 'now', or a number (Julian day, or Unix time with 'unixepoch'); 'now' when left out.

params.name: modifier
params.doc: Applied left to right: '+7 days', '-3 hours', '+1 months', 'start of month', 'start of year', 'start of day', 'weekday N', 'unixepoch', 'julianday', 'auto', 'localtime', 'utc', 'subsec', 'ceiling', 'floor'.

functions.name: strftime
functions.summary: Formats a date and time as text using a format string, after applying any modifiers.

params.name: format
params.doc: Substitutions: %Y year, %m month, %d day, %H hour, %M minute, %S seconds, %f fractional seconds, %s Unix time, %j day of year, %w weekday 0-6, %W week, %J Julian day, %F date, %T time, %% percent.

params.name: time_value
params.doc: A date/time string such as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', 'now', or a number (Julian day, or Unix time with 'unixepoch'); 'now' when left out.

params.name: modifier
params.doc: Applied left to right: '+7 days', '-3 hours', '+1 months', 'start of month', 'start of year', 'start of day', 'weekday N', 'unixepoch', 'julianday', 'auto', 'localtime', 'utc', 'subsec', 'ceiling', 'floor'.

functions.name: timediff
functions.summary: Returns the time from the second date/time to the first as text of the form +YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.SSS, suitable as a modifier (3.43+).

params.name: time_value_a
params.doc: The later (or end) date/time.

params.name: time_value_b
params.doc: The date/time to subtract.

functions.name: CURRENT_DATE
functions.summary: Returns the current UTC date as text in the form YYYY-MM-DD. Written without parentheses.

functions.name: CURRENT_TIME
functions.summary: Returns the current UTC time as text in the form HH:MM:SS. Written without parentheses.

functions.name: CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
functions.summary: Returns the current UTC date and time as text in the form YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. Written without parentheses; use datetime('now', 'localtime') for local time.

functions.name: acos
functions.summary: Returns the arc cosine of a number, in radians. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: x
params.doc: A value from -1 to 1.

functions.name: acosh
functions.summary: Returns the inverse hyperbolic cosine of a number. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: x
params.doc: A value of 1 or more.

functions.name: asin
functions.summary: Returns the arc sine of a number, in radians. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: x
params.doc: A value from -1 to 1.

functions.name: asinh
functions.summary: Returns the inverse hyperbolic sine of a number. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: x
params.doc: The input value.

functions.name: atan
functions.summary: Returns the arc tangent of a number, in radians. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: x
params.doc: The input value.

functions.name: atan2
functions.summary: Returns the arc tangent of y/x in radians, using the signs of both to pick the quadrant. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: y
params.doc: The y coordinate (numerator).

params.name: x
params.doc: The x coordinate (denominator).

functions.name: atanh
functions.summary: Returns the inverse hyperbolic tangent of a number. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: x
params.doc: A value between -1 and 1.

functions.name: ceil
functions.summary: Returns the smallest integer value not less than the argument; integers are returned unchanged. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: x
params.doc: The input value.

functions.name: ceiling
functions.summary: Alias of ceil: returns the smallest integer value not less than the argument. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: x
params.doc: The input value.

functions.name: cos
functions.summary: Returns the cosine of an angle given in radians. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: x
params.doc: Angle in radians.

functions.name: cosh
functions.summary: Returns the hyperbolic cosine of a number. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: x
params.doc: The input value.

functions.name: degrees
functions.summary: Converts an angle from radians to degrees. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: x
params.doc: Angle in radians.

functions.name: exp
functions.summary: Returns e raised to the given power. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: x
params.doc: The exponent.

functions.name: floor
functions.summary: Returns the largest integer value not greater than the argument; integers are returned unchanged. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: x
params.doc: The input value.

functions.name: ln
functions.summary: Returns the natural (base-e) logarithm of a number. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: x
params.doc: A positive value.

functions.name: log
functions.summary: With one argument, returns the base-10 logarithm (not the natural log; use ln for that). With two, returns the logarithm of x in the given base. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: x
params.doc: A positive value.

params.name: base
params.doc: The logarithm base; comes first.

params.name: x
params.doc: A positive value.

functions.name: log10
functions.summary: Returns the base-10 logarithm of a number. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: x
params.doc: A positive value.

functions.name: log2
functions.summary: Returns the base-2 logarithm of a number. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: x
params.doc: A positive value.

functions.name: mod
functions.summary: Returns the remainder of dividing x by y; like the % operator but also works on non-integer values. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: x
params.doc: The dividend.

params.name: y
params.doc: The divisor.

functions.name: pi
functions.summary: Returns an approximation of pi. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

functions.name: pow
functions.summary: Returns x raised to the power y. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: x
params.doc: The base.

params.name: y
params.doc: The exponent.

functions.name: power
functions.summary: Alias of pow: returns x raised to the power y. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: x
params.doc: The base.

params.name: y
params.doc: The exponent.

functions.name: radians
functions.summary: Converts an angle from degrees to radians. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: x
params.doc: Angle in degrees.

functions.name: sin
functions.summary: Returns the sine of an angle given in radians. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: x
params.doc: Angle in radians.

functions.name: sinh
functions.summary: Returns the hyperbolic sine of a number. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: x
params.doc: The input value.

functions.name: sqrt
functions.summary: Returns the square root of a number, or NULL for a negative number. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: x
params.doc: A non-negative value.

functions.name: tan
functions.summary: Returns the tangent of an angle given in radians. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: x
params.doc: Angle in radians.

functions.name: tanh
functions.summary: Returns the hyperbolic tangent of a number. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: x
params.doc: The input value.

functions.name: trunc
functions.summary: Returns the integer part of a number, rounding toward zero; integers are returned unchanged. Built-in math function (3.35+, when compiled with math functions).

params.name: x
params.doc: The input value.

functions.name: json
functions.summary: Validates JSON (or JSONB) input and returns it as minified canonical JSON text; raises an error if it is not well-formed.

params.name: json
params.doc: JSON text or a JSONB BLOB.

functions.name: jsonb
functions.summary: Converts JSON text (or JSONB) into the binary JSONB format; raises an error if it is not well-formed (3.45+).

params.name: json
params.doc: JSON text or a JSONB BLOB.

functions.name: json_array
functions.summary: Returns a JSON array built from its arguments; text arguments become JSON strings unless they come from another JSON function.

params.name: value
params.doc: An element of the array; add more arguments for more elements.

functions.name: jsonb_array
functions.summary: Like json_array, but returns the array in the binary JSONB format (3.45+).

params.name: value
params.doc: An element of the array; add more arguments for more elements.

functions.name: json_array_length
functions.summary: Returns the number of elements in a JSON array, 0 if the value is not an array, or NULL if the path does not exist.

params.name: json
params.doc: JSON text or a JSONB BLOB.

params.name: path
params.doc: A JSON path such as '$.items'; the whole document when left out.

functions.name: json_error_position
functions.summary: Returns 0 if the input is well-formed JSON or JSONB, otherwise the 1-based character (or byte) position of the first syntax error (3.42+).

params.name: json
params.doc: JSON text or a JSONB BLOB.

functions.name: json_extract
functions.summary: Extracts the value at a path as an SQL value (text, number or NULL; objects and arrays as JSON text). With several paths, returns a JSON array of the results.

params.name: json
params.doc: JSON text or a JSONB BLOB.

params.name: path
params.doc: A JSON path such as '$.a.b[0]'; add more paths to get a JSON array of results.

functions.name: jsonb_extract
functions.summary: Like json_extract, but returns objects and arrays in the binary JSONB format (3.45+).

functions.name: bm25
functions.summary: FTS5 auxiliary function returning the BM25 relevance of the current match; smaller (more negative) is better, so ORDER BY bm25(t) puts the best first.
functions.example: SELECT * FROM docs WHERE docs MATCH 'sqlite' ORDER BY bm25(docs)

params.name: fts_table
params.doc: The FTS5 table named in the MATCH.

params.name: weight
params.doc: Weight for each column in order; add one argument per column. Columns default to 1.0.

functions.name: highlight

params.name: fts_table
params.doc: The FTS5 table named in the MATCH.

params.name: column
params.doc: 0-based index of the column to return.

params.name: open_text
params.doc: Text inserted before each match.

params.name: close_text
params.doc: Text inserted after each match.

functions.name: snippet
functions.summary: FTS5 auxiliary function returning a short fragment of a column around the matches, with matches wrapped in markers and trimmed text marked by an ellipsis.

params.name: fts_table
params.doc: The FTS5 table named in the MATCH.

params.name: column
params.doc: 0-based index of the column to take the fragment from; -1 picks the best column.

params.name: open_text
params.doc: Text inserted before each match.

params.name: close_text
params.doc: Text inserted after each match.

params.name: ellipsis
params.doc: Text added where the fragment is cut off.

params.name: max_tokens
params.doc: Maximum number of tokens in the fragment, from 1 to 64.

keywords.name: LIMIT
keywords.doc: Caps the number of rows a query returns; an optional OFFSET skips rows first. LIMIT -1 means no limit.
keywords.syntax: LIMIT count [OFFSET skip] | LIMIT skip, count

keywords.name: OFFSET
keywords.doc: Skips the given number of rows before LIMIT starts counting.

keywords.name: IF
keywords.doc: Begins an IF EXISTS or IF NOT EXISTS guard on CREATE or DROP statements.
keywords.syntax: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS name (…)

keywords.name: IF EXISTS
keywords.doc: Makes a DROP statement do nothing, instead of failing, when the object does not exist.

keywords.name: IF NOT EXISTS
keywords.doc: Makes a CREATE statement do nothing, instead of failing, when an object with that name already exists.
keywords.syntax: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS name (…)

keywords.name: TEMP
keywords.doc: Creates a table, view or trigger in the temp database, private to the connection and dropped when it closes. Same as TEMPORARY.

keywords.name: TEMPORARY
keywords.doc: Creates a table, view or trigger in the temp database, private to the connection and dropped when it closes.

keywords.name: AUTOINCREMENT
keywords.doc: On an INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, prevents rowids of deleted rows from being reused, tracking the highest value in sqlite_sequence. Usually unnecessary.

keywords.name: WITHOUT ROWID
keywords.doc: Creates a table stored as a clustered index on its PRIMARY KEY, with no hidden rowid column. The table must declare a PRIMARY KEY.
keywords.syntax: CREATE TABLE name (…, PRIMARY KEY (a, b)) WITHOUT ROWID

keywords.name: ROWID
keywords.doc: The hidden 64-bit integer key of every ordinary table, also reachable as _rowid_ or oid. A column declared INTEGER PRIMARY KEY is an alias for it.

keywords.name: STRICT
keywords.doc: Table option that enforces declared column types: values must match INT, INTEGER, REAL, TEXT, BLOB or ANY, or the insert fails (3.37+).

keywords.name: PRAGMA
keywords.doc: Reads or changes an SQLite setting or queries internal metadata, such as foreign_keys, journal_mode or table_info.

keywords.name: ATTACH
keywords.doc: Opens another database file on this connection under a schema name, so its tables can be queried as schema.table.

keywords.name: DETACH
keywords.doc: Closes a database previously added with ATTACH.

keywords.name: DATABASE
keywords.doc: Optional word in ATTACH DATABASE and DETACH DATABASE.

keywords.name: VACUUM
keywords.doc: Rebuilds the database file to reclaim free space and defragment it; VACUUM INTO writes a compacted copy to a new file instead.

keywords.name: ANALYZE
keywords.doc: Gathers statistics about tables and indexes into sqlite_stat tables so the query planner can choose better plans.

keywords.name: REINDEX
keywords.doc: Deletes and rebuilds indexes, for example after a collation's definition changes.

keywords.name: EXPLAIN
keywords.doc: Shows the virtual machine bytecode a statement compiles to instead of running it.

keywords.name: EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN
keywords.doc: Shows the high-level strategy SQLite will use for a statement: which tables are scanned, which indexes are used, and in what order.

keywords.name: GLOB
keywords.doc: Case-sensitive pattern match using Unix wildcards: * any run of characters, ? one character, [...] a character set.

keywords.name: REGEXP
keywords.doc: Regular-expression match operator. It calls a user function named regexp(), which is not built in; it errors unless the application or an extension provides one.

keywords.name: MATCH
keywords.doc: Full-text search operator for FTS3/FTS4/FTS5 virtual tables; ordinary tables have no MATCH implementation.

keywords.name: ISNULL
keywords.doc: Postfix operator that is true when the expression is NULL; same as IS NULL.

keywords.name: NOTNULL
keywords.doc: Postfix operator that is true when the expression is not NULL; same as IS NOT NULL.

keywords.name: CONFLICT
keywords.doc: Names the conflict-resolution algorithm of a constraint (ON CONFLICT ROLLBACK | ABORT | FAIL | IGNORE | REPLACE) or starts an upsert clause.

keywords.name: ON CONFLICT
keywords.doc: In a constraint, sets how violations are resolved. After INSERT … VALUES, starts an upsert: DO NOTHING, or DO UPDATE SET using the excluded row.
keywords.syntax: INSERT … ON CONFLICT [(column, …)] DO NOTHING | DO UPDATE SET column = excluded.column

keywords.name: OR REPLACE
keywords.doc: On INSERT or UPDATE, deletes the existing rows that would violate a UNIQUE or PRIMARY KEY constraint, then proceeds.

keywords.name: OR IGNORE
keywords.doc: On INSERT or UPDATE, silently skips any row that would violate a constraint and continues with the rest.

keywords.name: OR ABORT
keywords.doc: On INSERT or UPDATE, stops the statement and undoes its changes on a constraint violation, keeping the transaction. The default.

keywords.name: OR FAIL
keywords.doc: On INSERT or UPDATE, stops the statement on a constraint violation but keeps the changes it had already made.

keywords.name: OR ROLLBACK
keywords.doc: On INSERT or UPDATE, rolls back the whole transaction on a constraint violation.

keywords.name: REPLACE INTO
keywords.doc: Shorthand for INSERT OR REPLACE INTO: rows that would violate a UNIQUE or PRIMARY KEY constraint are deleted before the insert.

keywords.name: ABORT
keywords.doc: Conflict algorithm that aborts the current statement and reverts its changes; also a RAISE action in triggers.

keywords.name: FAIL
keywords.doc: Conflict algorithm that stops the current statement but keeps its earlier changes; also a RAISE action in triggers.

keywords.name: IGNORE
keywords.doc: Conflict algorithm that skips the offending row; in a trigger, RAISE(IGNORE) abandons the current row silently.

keywords.name: RETURNING
keywords.doc: Makes INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE return the affected rows, like a SELECT on the changed data (3.35+).

keywords.name: DO UPDATE
keywords.doc: Upsert action: when the insert conflicts, updates the existing row instead. The proposed row is available as excluded.
keywords.syntax: ON CONFLICT (column) DO UPDATE SET column = excluded.column [WHERE …]

keywords.name: DO NOTHING
keywords.doc: Upsert action: when the insert conflicts, skips the row.

keywords.name: EXCLUDED
keywords.doc: In an upsert's DO UPDATE clause, the table-name qualifier for the row that was proposed for insertion.

keywords.name: DEFAULT VALUES
keywords.doc: Inserts one row with every column set to its default value.

keywords.name: DEFERRABLE
keywords.doc: Marks a foreign key so that, with INITIALLY DEFERRED, it is checked at COMMIT instead of after each statement.

keywords.name: NOT DEFERRABLE
keywords.doc: Marks a foreign key as checked immediately after each statement. The default.

keywords.name: INITIALLY DEFERRED
keywords.doc: With DEFERRABLE, defers foreign key checks to COMMIT. PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys can do the same per transaction.

keywords.name: INITIALLY IMMEDIATE
keywords.doc: With DEFERRABLE, checks the foreign key after each statement. The default.

keywords.name: DEFERRED
keywords.doc: Transaction mode that takes no locks until the database is first read or written. The default for BEGIN.

keywords.name: IMMEDIATE
keywords.doc: Transaction mode that starts a write transaction at once, so other writers wait or get SQLITE_BUSY.

keywords.name: EXCLUSIVE
keywords.doc: Transaction mode that starts a write transaction at once and, outside WAL mode, also blocks other readers.

keywords.name: RELEASE
keywords.doc: Commits a savepoint and every savepoint started after it, removing them from the transaction stack.

keywords.name: TO
keywords.doc: Used in ROLLBACK TO savepoint and RENAME TO.

keywords.name: RAISE
keywords.doc: In a trigger body, raises an error or abandons the row: RAISE(IGNORE), or RAISE(ROLLBACK | ABORT | FAIL, 'message').
keywords.syntax: RAISE(IGNORE | ROLLBACK, msg | ABORT, msg | FAIL, msg)

keywords.name: INSTEAD OF
keywords.doc: Trigger timing for views: the trigger body runs in place of the INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE on the view.
keywords.syntax: CREATE TRIGGER name INSTEAD OF INSERT ON view BEGIN … END

keywords.name: BEFORE
keywords.doc: Trigger timing: the body runs before the row is changed.
keywords.syntax: CREATE TRIGGER name BEFORE INSERT ON table BEGIN … END

keywords.name: AFTER
keywords.doc: Trigger timing: the body runs after the row is changed. The default.
keywords.syntax: CREATE TRIGGER name AFTER UPDATE ON table BEGIN … END

keywords.name: FOR EACH ROW
keywords.doc: Trigger granularity; SQLite only supports row triggers, so this is implied when left out.
keywords.syntax: CREATE TRIGGER name AFTER INSERT ON table FOR EACH ROW BEGIN … END

keywords.name: OF
keywords.doc: Limits an UPDATE trigger to changes of the listed columns.
keywords.syntax: CREATE TRIGGER name AFTER UPDATE OF column, … ON table …

keywords.name: NEW
keywords.doc: In a trigger body, the row as it will be (INSERT/UPDATE).

keywords.name: OLD
keywords.doc: In a trigger body, the row as it was (UPDATE/DELETE).

keywords.name: VIRTUAL
keywords.doc: CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE makes a table backed by a module such as fts5 or rtree; in a generated column, VIRTUAL computes the value on read (the default).
keywords.syntax: CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE name USING fts5(column, …)

keywords.name: GENERATED ALWAYS
keywords.doc: Declares a generated column computed from other columns of the row, either VIRTUAL (computed on read) or STORED (3.31+).
keywords.syntax: column type GENERATED ALWAYS AS (expression) [VIRTUAL | STORED]

keywords.name: STORED
keywords.doc: Generated column that is computed on write and saved in the table.

keywords.name: WINDOW
keywords.doc: Names a window definition once so several window functions can share it with OVER name.
keywords.syntax: WINDOW name AS (PARTITION BY … ORDER BY …)

keywords.name: FILTER
keywords.doc: Limits the rows an aggregate or aggregate window function sees.

keywords.name: GROUPS
keywords.doc: Window frame unit that counts peer groups (rows with equal ORDER BY values) rather than rows or values.
keywords.syntax: GROUPS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW

keywords.name: EXCLUDE
keywords.doc: Removes rows from a window frame: EXCLUDE NO OTHERS (default), EXCLUDE CURRENT ROW, EXCLUDE GROUP or EXCLUDE TIES.
keywords.syntax: ROWS BETWEEN … AND … EXCLUDE CURRENT ROW | GROUP | TIES | NO OTHERS

keywords.name: NULLS FIRST
keywords.doc: Sorts NULLs before other values; the default for ascending order in SQLite (3.30+).
keywords.syntax: ORDER BY expression [ASC | DESC] NULLS FIRST

keywords.name: NULLS LAST
keywords.doc: Sorts NULLs after other values; the default for descending order in SQLite (3.30+).
keywords.syntax: ORDER BY expression [ASC | DESC] NULLS LAST

keywords.name: RECURSIVE
keywords.doc: Allows a common table expression to refer to itself, for walking trees and generating series.
keywords.syntax: WITH RECURSIVE name(column) AS (initial UNION ALL SELECT … FROM name …) SELECT …

keywords.name: MATERIALIZED
keywords.doc: Forces a common table expression to be computed once into a temporary table.

keywords.name: NOT MATERIALIZED
keywords.doc: Asks the planner to inline a common table expression into the query like a subquery.

keywords.name: INDEXED BY
keywords.doc: Requires the query to use the named index on that table; the statement fails if it cannot.

keywords.name: NOT INDEXED
keywords.doc: Prevents the query from using any index on that table (the rowid or primary key may still be used).

keywords.name: RENAME
keywords.doc: ALTER TABLE action that renames a table or a column.
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE name RENAME [COLUMN] old TO new

keywords.name: RENAME TO
keywords.doc: Renames a table.
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE name RENAME TO new_name

keywords.name: RENAME COLUMN
keywords.doc: Renames a column; references in indexes, triggers and views are updated (3.25+).
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE name RENAME COLUMN old TO new

keywords.name: DROP COLUMN
keywords.doc: Removes a column from a table; fails if the column is indexed, in a key or constraint, or referenced elsewhere (3.35+).
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE name DROP COLUMN column

keywords.name: IS DISTINCT FROM
keywords.doc: Null-safe inequality: true when the values differ, treating two NULLs as equal. Same as IS NOT (3.39+).

keywords.name: IS NOT DISTINCT FROM
keywords.doc: Null-safe equality: true when the values are equal or both NULL. Same as IS (3.39+).
keywords.syntax: a IS NOT DISTINCT FROM b

keywords.name: ON DELETE
keywords.doc: Foreign key action taken when the parent row is deleted: NO ACTION (default), RESTRICT, SET NULL, SET DEFAULT or CASCADE.

keywords.name: ON UPDATE
keywords.doc: Foreign key action taken when the parent key changes: NO ACTION (default), RESTRICT, SET NULL, SET DEFAULT or CASCADE.

keywords.name: CASCADE
keywords.doc: Foreign key action that deletes or updates the child rows along with the parent row.

keywords.name: RESTRICT
keywords.doc: Foreign key action that forbids deleting or changing a parent key while child rows reference it, checked immediately.

keywords.name: NO ACTION
keywords.doc: Foreign key action that does nothing special; the constraint is simply checked at the end of the statement. The default.

keywords.name: SET DEFAULT
keywords.doc: Foreign key action that sets the child's key columns to their default values.

keywords.name: NOCASE
keywords.doc: Built-in collation that compares text ignoring the case of ASCII letters.

keywords.name: BINARY
keywords.doc: Built-in collation that compares text byte by byte with memcmp. The default.

constants.name: TRUE
constants.doc: The integer 1. SQLite has no separate boolean type; TRUE is an alias for 1 (3.23+).

constants.name: FALSE
constants.doc: The integer 0. SQLite has no separate boolean type; FALSE is an alias for 0 (3.23+).

types.name: INTEGER
types.doc: INTEGER affinity; values are stored as signed integers of up to 8 bytes. A column declared exactly INTEGER PRIMARY KEY becomes an alias for the rowid. Allowed in STRICT tables.

types.name: INT
types.doc: INTEGER affinity (any type name containing INT). Signed integers up to 8 bytes. Unlike INTEGER, INT PRIMARY KEY does not alias the rowid. Allowed in STRICT tables.

types.name: TINYINT
types.doc: INTEGER affinity; the size is not enforced, so any 64-bit integer fits.

types.name: SMALLINT
types.doc: INTEGER affinity; the size is not enforced, so any 64-bit integer fits.

types.name: MEDIUMINT
types.doc: INTEGER affinity; the size is not enforced, so any 64-bit integer fits.

types.name: BIGINT
types.doc: INTEGER affinity; signed integers up to 8 bytes.

types.name: REAL
types.doc: REAL affinity; values are stored as 8-byte IEEE floating-point numbers. Allowed in STRICT tables.

types.name: DOUBLE
types.doc: REAL affinity (any type name containing DOUB); 8-byte IEEE floating point. DOUBLE PRECISION is the same.

types.name: FLOAT
types.doc: REAL affinity (any type name containing FLOA); 8-byte IEEE floating point regardless of precision.

types.name: NUMERIC
types.doc: NUMERIC affinity: text that looks like a number is stored as INTEGER or REAL; other values are kept as they are. Precision and scale are ignored.

types.name: DECIMAL
types.doc: NUMERIC affinity; precision and scale are ignored and values are stored as INTEGER or REAL, not exact decimals.

types.name: BOOLEAN
types.doc: NUMERIC affinity; there is no boolean storage class, so values are stored as the integers 1 (TRUE) and 0 (FALSE).

types.name: DATE
types.doc: NUMERIC affinity; there is no date storage class. Store dates as ISO-8601 text, Julian day REAL or Unix-time INTEGER and use the date functions.

types.name: DATETIME
types.doc: NUMERIC affinity; there is no date/time storage class. Store values as ISO-8601 text ('YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'), Julian day REAL or Unix-time INTEGER.

types.name: TEXT
types.doc: TEXT affinity; values are stored as strings in the database encoding (UTF-8 or UTF-16), and numbers inserted are converted to text. Allowed in STRICT tables.

types.name: VARCHAR
types.doc: TEXT affinity (contains CHAR); the length is not enforced.

types.name: CHAR
types.doc: TEXT affinity; the length is not enforced and values are not padded.

types.name: NCHAR
types.doc: TEXT affinity (contains CHAR); the length is not enforced.

types.name: NVARCHAR
types.doc: TEXT affinity (contains CHAR); the length is not enforced.

types.name: CLOB
types.doc: TEXT affinity (contains CLOB); no size limit beyond SQLite's maximum string length.

types.name: BLOB
types.doc: BLOB affinity: values are stored exactly as given, with no conversion. A column with no declared type has the same affinity. Allowed in STRICT tables.

types.name: ANY
types.doc: In a STRICT table, accepts any value and stores it unchanged. In an ordinary table, ANY gets NUMERIC affinity, so numeric-looking text is converted.
